clauses.clause: Develop group norms for participation in a community of readers and writers
clauses.note: Students review an existing anchor chart; they do not create norms.

clauses.clause: Discuss texts with others in the group
clauses.note: Students discuss content knowledge and practice presentations, but there is no clear discussion of specific texts.

clauses.clause: Share individual writing with the group
clauses.note: Students practice sharing their own poems with partners.

clauses.clause: Listen to others as they share their writing
clauses.note: Partner sharing implies taking turns listening; students are prompted to listen as others share.

clauses.clause: Offer feedback on peers' writing
clauses.note: No peer feedback on writing is included.

clauses.clause: Respond to feedback received on own writing
clauses.note: No activity directs students to respond to feedback.

verdicts.evidence: Tell students that they will now practice sharing their poems with a partner so that they are prepared to share them when the visitors come. Tell students they will use the Pinky Partners protocol to practice sharing their poems. Remind them that they used this protocol in previous lessons and review as necessary using the Pinky Partners Protocol anchor chart. (Refer to the Classroom Protocols document for the full version of the protocol.) Distribute students' 'What the Sun Sees' poems. Invite students to begin the Pinky Partners protocol. Circulate as students share, directing students' attention to the Ways We Share Our Work anchor chart as necessary and making note of progress toward SL.1.4 and SL.1.6 using the Speaking and Listening Checklist.
verdicts.rationale: Students practice sharing their own writing with partners and listening during partner sharing. They do not develop group norms, discuss specific texts, or engage in giving/receiving feedback on writing.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Participate in a community of readers and writers by developing group norms, discussing texts, sharing individual writing, listening as others share their writing, and offering and responding to feedback. (I/C)

clauses.note: Students revisit and recite the Sun and Moon songs with accompanying motions.

verdicts.evidence:
Tell students that they have one more piece of work to share with their visitors: their 'What the Sun Sees' poems.
Direct students' attention to the posted learning targets and read the second one aloud:
'I can read my writing aloud using a strong and clear voice.'
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
'When you are sharing your poems, what is important to remember to do so that your visitors can learn from you?' (speak clearly and loudly, make eye contact with visitors, listen as others share)
Tell students that they will now practice sharing their poems with a partner so that they are prepared to share them when the visitors come.
Distribute students' 'What the Sun Sees' poems.
Invite students to begin the Pinky Partners protocol.
verdicts.rationale: Students practice presenting clearly and tailoring to visitors (voice, eye contact) and recite songs, but the lesson does not have students engage in full audience Q&A (asking and answering). [REJECTED: evidence missing or not found in lesson raw text]

clauses.clause: Work with others to discuss topics, investigate questions, solve problems, and explore and create texts.
clauses.note: Students work with partners to discuss topics and answer questions using structured protocols.

verdicts.evidence:
Tell students they are going to use the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face protocol to discuss the answers to questions about the sun, moon, and stars and what they have learned. Remind them that they used this protocol in previous lessons and review as necessary using the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face Protocol anchor chart. (Refer to the Classroom Protocols document for the full version of the protocol.)
- Guide students through four rounds of the protocol using the following questions:
- 'What is a pattern that the sun, moon, or stars follow? How would you describe that pattern?'
- 'What is something you learned about the sun, moon, or stars that you did not know before?'
- 'What do you still wonder about the sun, moon, or stars?'
- 'What did you learn about the Unit 3 guiding question: How do writers use their knowledge and observations to write a story?'
- As students talk, circulate and listen in. Take note of the ideas they are sharing and target a few students to share out with the whole group.
verdicts.rationale: Students collaborate through structured partner protocols to discuss and share ideas, aligning with collaborative discussion aspects. However, they do not co-establish norms or jointly complete a shared project, so full alignment is not demonstrated.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
